analytics.help:
Worker: read this run's own usage-counts and spend summaries over a window —
the routine and scope are both derived server-side from the worker's own lease, so
no verb here takes a flag naming either.
analytics.short_help: Worker: read this run's own usage-counts and spend summaries over a window — the routine and scope are both derived server-side from the worker's own lease, so no verb here takes a flag naming either.

commit.help:
Worker: durably declare a git-commit artifact for REPO (issue #143). Carries the ``git_commit``
kind only — an asset is declared through ``artifact create``. Node scope only. Deliberately no
``--forge``: the origin comes from the environment's repo manifest (pinned by
tests/test_runner_artifact_commit_cli.py::test_commit_verb_has_no_forge_flag). Echoes a
confirmation naming REPO, BRANCH, and the sha on success (issue #584) — a silent exit 0 was
indistinguishable from a no-op.
commit.short_help: Worker: durably declare a git-commit artifact for REPO (issue #143).

create.help:
Worker: durably submit an asset artifact for a ``produces:`` NAME (content on stdin), node
scope only. A submission *stages* the content, published into the envelope only on completion
(issue #169) — read it back with ``artifact staged``. Empty stdin and any rejection exit
non-zero rather than silently losing the submission.
create.short_help: Worker: durably submit an asset artifact for a ``produces:`` NAME (content on stdin), node scope only.

get.help:
Worker: read one artifact by NAME — a ``produces:`` name (node scope), a baked-in graph
declaration (graph scope), or one of blizzard's own published documents (system scope);
unknown is a ``404``, more than one candidate a ``409`` naming them. ``--content`` prints
raw asset text, and errors on the ``git_commit`` kind, which carries none.

Serves the last *published* epoch only — a node-step's own just-submitted content is not
published until the node-step completes; a not-yet-published NAME 404s naming
``artifact staged`` instead. Read it back before completion with that verb.

NAME is passed literally: the CLI percent-encodes it itself (issue #233), slashes
included, so a slashed name (e.g. a ``merged/<owner>/<repo>`` delivery marker) is passed
as-is, not pre-encoded.
get.short_help: Worker: read one artifact by NAME — a ``produces:`` name (node scope), a baked-in graph declaration (graph scope), or one of blizzard's own published documents (system scope); unknown is a ``404``, more than one candidate a ``409`` naming them.

list.help:
Worker: list this node-step's artifacts as kind-discriminated JSON, resolved latest-by-epoch,
plus the graph mint's own baked-in declarations and blizzard's published system-artifact
set — ``--scope`` narrows to one. Content is elided by default (issue #169), since inlining
every upstream asset's full text has overflowed tool output; ``--content`` restores it.
Also includes this node-step's own staged, not-yet-published submissions (issue #584),
each carrying ``"staged": true`` — everything published carries ``"staged": false``.
list.short_help: Worker: list this node-step's artifacts as kind-discriminated JSON, resolved latest-by-epoch, plus the graph mint's own baked-in declarations and blizzard's published system-artifact set — ``--scope`` narrows to one.

staged.help:
Worker: list this node-step's own staged (not-yet-published) submissions, node scope only.
Read straight off the runner's own ``attachments`` record rather than the hub envelope (issue
#169), so a fresh ``artifact create`` shows up here immediately; ``--content`` gives the full
text.
staged.short_help: Worker: list this node-step's own staged (not-yet-published) submissions, node scope only.

artifact.help:
Worker: read node-step, graph, and system artifacts; write this node-step's own (issue
#127). The lease binding is ambient: every verb acts on the worker's own lease, resolved
from the spawn environment — none takes a flag naming another chunk. ``--scope`` picks node
scope, the graph mint's baked-in declarations, or blizzard's published system-artifact set.
``create`` *stages* a submission, published on completion (#169).
artifact.short_help: Worker: read node-step, graph, and system artifacts; write this node-step's own (issue #127).

ask.help: Worker: ask-and-exit — the ask is a durable runner-store fact before this returns.
ask.short_help: Worker: ask-and-exit — the ask is a durable runner-store fact before this returns.

attach.help:
Deprecated alias for ``blizzard runner artifact create`` (issue #127).

Kept working, hidden from ``--help``: it warns on stderr and delegates with identical behavior.
attach.short_help: Deprecated alias for ``blizzard runner artifact create`` (issue #127).

history.help:
Worker: read this chunk's own transition history as kind-discriminated JSON (issue #237) — the
merged, oldest-first timeline, one row per accepted transition, cross-graph migration, or delivery
bounce, each carrying its own ``kind``. The in-flight node-step this call is part of is not
there yet: a transition is recorded only once an attempt completes.
history.short_help: Worker: read this chunk's own transition history as kind-discriminated JSON (issue #237) — the merged, oldest-first timeline, one row per accepted transition, cross-graph migration, or delivery bounce, each carrying its own ``kind``.

chunk.help: Worker: read facts about the chunk this node-step belongs to.
chunk.short_help: Worker: read facts about the chunk this node-step belongs to.

probe.help:
Sample one declared subscription's rate-limit usage, by SLUG, and print it.

Read-only, writes nothing. SLUG defaults to the legacy ``anthropic`` declaration
every runner still carries.
probe.short_help: Sample one declared subscription's rate-limit usage, by SLUG, and print it.

external-usage.help: Diagnostics for the runner's own external-subscription usage sampling (issue #218).
external-usage.short_help: Diagnostics for the runner's own external-subscription usage sampling (issue #218).

get.help:
Worker: read one finding within this chunk's own answered set by FINDING_ID, as
JSON — a key within the worker's own brief, the way ``artifact get NAME`` is a key
within its own node-step.
get.short_help: Worker: read one finding within this chunk's own answered set by FINDING_ID, as JSON — a key within the worker's own brief, the way ``artifact get NAME`` is a key within its own node-step.

list.short_help: Worker: list the findings this chunk's own accepted, minted garden proposal answers, as JSON.

proposals.short_help: Worker: list this run's own routine's garden proposals as JSON, filtered by STATE — closed ones carry their closure and pass reason.

garden.help:
Worker: read this run's own garden machinery — the routine and scope are both
derived server-side from the worker's own lease, so no verb here takes a flag
naming either.
garden.short_help: Worker: read this run's own garden machinery — the routine and scope are both derived server-side from the worker's own lease, so no verb here takes a flag naming either.

heartbeat.help:
Worker hook: record a lease heartbeat (identity from the environment).

Fails **soft**: a hook must never break the worker's tool call, so a missing identity or an
unreachable runner is reported to stderr and this still exits 0.
heartbeat.short_help: Worker hook: record a lease heartbeat (identity from the environment).

host.help:
Become the blizzard-runner daemon: the reconciliation loop + the local API.

DIRECTORY (positional) and --dir are equivalent — pass one; giving both requires
they agree. Defaults to $BZ_RUNNER_DIR, then the cwd.
host.short_help: Become the blizzard-runner daemon: the reconciliation loop + the local API.

init.help:
Scaffold config + data dir + a migrated store under DIRECTORY. Idempotent.

DIRECTORY defaults to $BZ_RUNNER_DIR, then the cwd.
init.short_help: Scaffold config + data dir + a migrated store under DIRECTORY.

migrate.help: Apply pending store migrations, or reverse with --down <rev>.
migrate.short_help: Apply pending store migrations, or reverse with --down <rev>.

compatibility.help: Prove an admitted OpenCode version in a disposable git repository and retain sanitized evidence.
compatibility.short_help: Prove an admitted OpenCode version in a disposable git repository and retain sanitized evidence.

opencode.help: Read-only diagnostics for OpenCode's admitted-version compatibility contract.
opencode.short_help: Read-only diagnostics for OpenCode's admitted-version compatibility contract.

pause.help:
Declarative control: pause this runner — it starts no new workers (issue #45). This runner's
**own** brake, a pure client of its local API, so it works with the hub unreachable: a stalled
worker is not killed, and an exhausted retry budget does not escalate, until it is cleared. No
retry is consumed, and a live worker is left alone — this is not a drain. Distinct from the hub's
brake, and each is cleared where it was set.
pause.short_help: Declarative control: pause this runner — it starts no new workers (issue #45).

diff.help:
Diff this runtime's effective workspace prompt against packaged sample NAME.

Effective means the lane a spawn reads: the store override when one stands, else the
configured knob. Exits 1 when they differ, so a deploy can check a forked copy for drift.
diff.short_help: Diff this runtime's effective workspace prompt against packaged sample NAME.

install.help:
Copy packaged sample NAME into the runtime root and point the config at the copy.

The forked shape: the config carries `workspace_prompt_file`, never the package knob, so
`prompt diff` has a local file to compare. Takes effect on the next runner restart.
install.short_help: Copy packaged sample NAME into the runtime root and point the config at the copy.

list.help: List the workspace-prompt samples shipped in this wheel.
list.short_help: List the workspace-prompt samples shipped in this wheel.

show.help: Print packaged sample NAME's prose to stdout.
show.short_help: Print packaged sample NAME's prose to stdout.

status.help:
Report which source the effective workspace prompt comes from, and how large it is.

Exits 1 when a source is configured but resolves to nothing — the shape a rollback to a
wheel that does not read the configured knob produces.
status.short_help: Report which source the effective workspace prompt comes from, and how large it is.

prompt.help: Operator: the packaged workspace-prompt samples, and which one this runtime uses.
prompt.short_help: Operator: the packaged workspace-prompt samples, and which one this runtime uses.

requeue.help:
Hand a needs_human chunk back to the fleet: a fresh attempt at its current node (issue #53).
Clears the chunk's local needs_human hold; a fresh attempt spawns at the current node on the
fleet's next pass. The route is never released and the chunk never re-enters the hub's queue.
Refused ``409`` while its takeover is still open, or while it is not parked needs_human.
requeue.short_help: Hand a needs_human chunk back to the fleet: a fresh attempt at its current node (issue #53).

list.help: Worker: list every scope (slug, description, retired) as JSON.
list.short_help: Worker: list every scope (slug, description, retired) as JSON.

scope.help: Worker: read the deployment's scope vocabulary.
scope.short_help: Worker: read the deployment's scope vocabulary.

selftest.help:
Adapter-drift canary before an unattended period (issue #54): exercises CODING_HARNESS against a
throwaway scratch repo — spawn with a pre-assigned session id, a trivial edit+commit, verdict
elicitation, an automated follow-up resume, and resume-command composition — touching no chunk,
lease, environment, or hub. Posts the run, polls it, prints each check, exits non-zero on failure.
selftest.short_help: Adapter-drift canary before an unattended period (issue #54): exercises CODING_HARNESS against a throwaway scratch repo — spawn with a pre-assigned session id, a trivial edit+commit, verdict elicitation, an automated follow-up resume, and resume-command composition — touching no chunk, lease, environment, or hub.

session-end.help:
Worker hook: record the session's exit (identity from the environment) — the worker's
"declared done" signal.

Fails **soft**, like the heartbeat.
session-end.short_help: Worker hook: record the session's exit (identity from the environment) — the worker's "declared done" signal.

start.help:
Declarative control: clear this runner's own pause brake — it resumes spawning (issue #45).

The counterpart to ``blizzard runner pause``, and local in the same way. It clears only
the local brake: a runner also paused at the hub stays paused until ``blizzard hub
runner resume <runner_id>`` clears that one too.
start.short_help: Declarative control: clear this runner's own pause brake — it resumes spawning (issue #45).

status.help:
The machine-local view: capacities, held environments, open asks, escalations, open takeovers
(issue #51). Every section is this runner's own local read, so the view renders fully with the
hub unreachable; hub reachability is itself reported, not assumed.
status.short_help: The machine-local view: capacities, held environments, open asks, escalations, open takeovers (issue #51).

takeover.help:
Take over a parked chunk: exec the interactive resume command in this terminal (issue #52). The
takeover fact is recorded before anything else runs, so no loop step can respawn or judge the
session while it is open; the lease token travels only in the response body and the exec, never
printed. ``--force`` supersedes a live worker attempt instead of refusing. An interrupted session
still closes the takeover.
takeover.short_help: Take over a parked chunk: exec the interactive resume command in this terminal (issue #52).

tick.help:
Run ONE synchronous reconciliation tick (REAP → PULL → FILL → ADVANCE).

The steppable-loop driver for tests and the e2e (``bzh:steppable-loop``): a single pass against the
live hub and workspace, then exit. Refuses on a store revision mismatch, like ``host``.
tick.short_help: Run ONE synchronous reconciliation tick (REAP → PULL → FILL → ADVANCE).

backfill.help:
Import worker transcripts predating the outbound lane, best-effort.

Driven from this runner's own lease records, never a sweep of the harness directory. Rerunnable:
an already-imported session is skipped, and one left unfinished resumes. Writes the store
directly, so run it as the runner's own user with its environment, and with the daemon stopped.
backfill.short_help: Import worker transcripts predating the outbound lane, best-effort.

reship.help:
Re-read SEGMENT_ID's session and ship it again under a new segment id.

For a segment the hub holds in a form this runner has outgrown — most often one an older,
smaller per-record cap shrank. The hub never overwrites an accepted record, so superseding
one means a second segment: BOTH then show on the board. Same operating rules as `backfill`.
reship.short_help: Re-read SEGMENT_ID's session and ship it again under a new segment id.

transcript.help: Operator: maintenance over this runner's own transcript lane (blizzard#250).
transcript.short_help: Operator: maintenance over this runner's own transcript lane (blizzard#250).

work-items.help:
Worker: pass-through read of a chunk's work items (runner -> hub -> vendor).

The items print as JSON, one entry per pointer.
work-items.short_help: Worker: pass-through read of a chunk's work items (runner -> hub -> vendor).
